# Acceptable-use insert: Library Assistant

> Template, not legal advice. District counsel must review it before the board adopts it.

An insert for the district's acceptable-use policy (AUP). Part A is for staff and families,
and Part B is for Students. Fill in each `[BLANK: …]` with district details.

**Where the tier names come from.** DPI's guidance uses *Human-Only* and *AI-assist* to label
tasks. Its quick use matrix lists brainstorming and outlining as "Yes (AI-assist)" with
"Disclose tool & how used," and high-stakes assessments as "Human-Only unless accommodation"
([DPI Policy & Governance](https://dpi.wi.gov/imt/ai-guidance/administrators/policy); see also
"Human-Only/AI-Assist task design" on
[DPI Administrators](https://dpi.wi.gov/imt/ai-guidance/administrators)). DPI does not publish
the three names below as a set of tiers. *AI-Optional* is this template's own label. It does
not appear in DPI's current AI guidance `[VERIFY: checked October 2026]`. A district that
wants a finer scale can use the six levels from Sheboygan Area School District that DPI hosts
([AI Levels](https://dpi.wi.gov/sites/default/files/imce/imt/pdf/Sheboygan_Area_School_District_AI_LEVELS.pdf)),
which run from "No AI" to "Full AI."

---

## Part A: Policy language

### A1. Task labels

Teachers label each assignment with one of three tiers before students begin:

| Tier | Meaning | Library Assistant |
|---|---|---|
| **Human-Only** (DPI) | The work is done without AI. This is the default for high-stakes assessments unless an accommodation requires support. | Not used for this task |
| **AI-Assist** (DPI) | AI may help with named steps, such as finding sources or brainstorming. The student does the thinking and the writing. | Allowed for the named steps; the student discloses it |
| **AI-Optional** (this template) | The student may choose whether to use AI. If they do, they disclose it. | Allowed; the student discloses it |

An unlabelled assignment is treated as `[BLANK: Human-Only]`.

### A2. Student disclosure

When AI helped with an assignment, students paste this at the end of their work. It is DPI's
assignment disclosure box ([DPI Ethical Use](https://dpi.wi.gov/imt/ai-guidance/educators/ethical-use)):

> AI Use: Tool: ____ • Purpose: ____ • What I kept/changed: ____ • Verification steps: ____ • Date used: ____

For the Library Assistant, the "Tool" line reads "Library Assistant," and "Verification steps"
names the Records it cited that the student checked.

### A3. The Library Assistant

1. Students use the Library Assistant only during supervised class time, with a Card their
   Teacher provides.
2. Cards carry no names. The assistant never receives a Student's name. The Teacher keeps a
   Roster linking Card numbers to Students. An adult uses it only to follow up on a Flag
   (Identification).
3. The Librarian can see conversations while they happen. Conversations are deleted at the end
   of the school day, except those attached to an open Flag. See the district retention rule
   `[BLANK: policy number]`.
4. Messages that suggest self-harm, abuse, bullying, or threats of violence are Flagged for an
   adult. The Student gets a reply that points them to a trusted adult and the 988 line.
   Flagging helps adults with their duty of care. It does not replace it.
5. Misusing a Card (sharing it, using another Student's Card, or trying to get around the
   assistant's limits) is handled under `[BLANK: existing conduct policy]`.

---

## Part B: Rules for Students

Print this on the back of the Card sheet, or post it near the library computers.

**Using your Library Card for the assistant**

- Your Card is yours for today's class. Don't share it or post a picture of it.
- Your Card doesn't have your name on it, and the assistant doesn't know who you are. Your
  teacher keeps a list of who had which card.
- Don't type your name, address, phone number, or anyone else's name.
- The librarian can see what you ask while class is going on.
- If you write something that sounds like you or someone else could be hurt, the assistant
  will tell you to talk to a trusted adult, and an adult at school will check on it. That is
  to help you, not to get you in trouble.
- The assistant can be wrong. Check the book or source it points to.
- Your chat is deleted at the end of the school day, unless an adult still needs to follow up
  on something you wrote.
- Your Card stops working when class ends. If you lose it, tell your teacher.
- If your teacher says an assignment is Human-Only, don't use the assistant for it. If you
  do use it, fill in the AI Use box.
